name: Atrani
label: Atrani
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Via Gabriele di Benedetto' (3 web pages); placed at the stretch of Via Gabriele di Benedetto nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap relation/40656: large area 'Atrani' (659 m across): previous pin kept, it lies inside.
notes: Tiny pastel village on the beach just east of Amalfi.

text.description: Atrani is a tiny seaside village tucked between two hills, and it photographs well because everything is packed into one frame: a small beach, an arcade, pastel houses stacked up the slope and a church dome rising above them. It is officially the smallest municipality in Italy, covering just 12 hectares, and about 832 people lived here in 2020. Long ago it was the twin of Amalfi and home to its leading families. The dukes of Amalfi were crowned here in the chapel of San Salvatore, and the cap used in the ceremony was called the "birecto". The village's old central square still opens onto the beach through an old passageway that was built to save boats from sea storms. For the best phone picture, don't shoot from the sand. Stand on Via Gabriele di Benedetto, the stretch beside the Amalfi Drive road, one flight of steps up from the beach. From there you look down over the beach, the arcade and the rooftops, with the church dome in view. It is a better angle than the beach itself. If you also want a close-up of the dome and bell tower above the pastel houses, you can take one from the beach, Spiaggia di Atrani. Take care when you stop beside the road, because the Amalfi Drive has narrow stretches without pavements.
text.geographic_location: Atrani is a separate village just east of Amalfi, in the valley between Civita Hill and Aureo Hill, with its houses running right down to the beach. The viewpoint is on the street beside the coastal road, just above the beach.
text.directions_text: Start from Amalfi and head east along the coast; Atrani is several minutes' drive away. Make your way to the beach end of the village, then climb one flight of steps up from the beach to Via Gabriele di Benedetto. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the whole scene of beach, arcade and village. Then try telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) to pick out the church dome and the colours of the houses.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Via Gabriele di Benedetto (stretch next to the Amalfi Drive road, one flight of steps up from the beach). An elevated overview of the beach, the arcade and the village, with the church dome visible. On the stretch next to the Amalfi Drive road, one flight of steps up from the beach. From here the village lies to the north-west, and you look over the beach and arcade with the church dome showing above the houses.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and put the beach along the lower third, with the dome near one of the upper crossing points. Keep the phone level so the buildings don't lean. If you want a different angle, the beach itself shows the arcade and the dome with the bell tower above the pastel houses.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the church or the front of the houses to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky doesn't wash out. At dusk, switch on night mode and hold the phone as still as you can.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Blue hour, when the village lights come on, is the time a guide recommends for the best light.

text.access_note: The viewpoint is an ordinary street beside a public road, but conditions can change, so check locally, and check the official site before you go if you want to visit the church.

name: Marina Grande
label: Marina Grande
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale' (1 web pages); placed at our map tiles: 'Cimitero Monumentale' (pois).
pin_note: Position from OSM N3431280691 (Marina Grande): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Main beach and harbour with views of the colourful town.

text.description:
Marina Grande is Amalfi's harbour and beach front, where boats sit at their moorings, and the pastel town buildings and steep cliffs rise straight behind. It photographs well because everything is layered: boats in the foreground, then the curve of the harbour, the houses, and the hillside above. The small beach with its teal and yellow umbrellas adds a bright splash of colour at water level.

Stand there and look south-west toward the marina, then use the layers of boats, harbour, houses and hillside to build your shot.

For a quieter, wider alternative, the Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale is a separate viewpoint on the walk up toward the cemetery. It gives more of a view of the whole town of Amalfi than of the marina alone, so treat it as an optional extra rather than the stand-here location. It is best walked early in the morning, before it gets hot. Take your time on the path, keep to the side so others can pass, and check each shot for stray bags or signs along the edge of the frame.
text.geographic_location: Marina Grande is on Amalfi's waterfront, along the harbour and small beach, with the town's buildings and cliffs rising behind it. The Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale is a separate, optional viewpoint on the walk toward the cemetery.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is given for this spot, so start from the centre of Amalfi town. If you want a quieter, wider view of the town, the Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale is a separate optional walk, best done early in the morning. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the marina and its surroundings together. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want more of the hillside and sea. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out boats and the umbrellas on the beach.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale (the walk up toward the cemetery). The town of Amalfi seen from above, with the harbour visible below, though this view is mainly of the town rather than the marina alone. If you want a quieter, wider picture of the whole town, the Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale on the walk toward the cemetery is a separate alternative viewpoint.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on gridlines and place the harbour edge on a lower third line, with the buildings filling the middle and sky above. Keep the horizon level. Frame the curve of the harbour with boats in the foreground, or the small beach with its teal and yellow umbrellas and the town behind.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the marina to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the sky keeps its colour and the sea does not wash out. Try panorama for the full sweep of the harbour, moving slowly and keeping the phone level.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, before it gets hot, when the light is usually softer and the path to the optional belvedere is more comfortable and quieter.

text.access_note: The optional walk up toward the cemetery is a public path with no charge as far as we know; the cemetery itself may have its own visiting rules, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Marina Grande is the harbour and beach front of Amalfi town.
Early-morning light is usually softer and the view is often less hazy than later in the day.
The path up toward the cemetery is a public path where people may need to pass, so keeping to the side is considerate.
The cemetery may have its own visiting rules.
The marina is about 2 minutes on foot from the stand-here point.

name: Amalfi Cathedral
label: Amalfi Cathedral
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Piazza Duomo' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Piazza Duomo' (way/191471192): middle (61 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/254643211: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Duomo di Amalfi' (76 m across).
notes: Striped Arab-Norman façade at the top of a grand staircase.

text.description: Amalfi Cathedral (the Duomo di Amalfi, dedicated to Saint Andrew) is the centrepiece of Piazza del Duomo, and guides treat its striped facade as the standard postcard view. A wide, steep flight of 62 steps leads up to the doors, which gives you a natural frame for a photo. The facade you see today is fairly young. Part of the earlier front collapsed in 1861, and the whole face was rebuilt in a richly decorated Arab-Norman and Gothic style, finished in 1891. The mosaic-topped pediment and the banded marble and stone are the main reasons it looks so good on a small screen. Beside it rises the bell tower, begun in 1180 and finished over a century later. Its crown of small towers is covered in bright majolica tiles. The bronze doors are older still, cast in Constantinople before 1066. From the foot of the steps you can fit the facade, the tower and the steps in one shot, with the square's fountain and people in the foreground to show the scale. Late afternoon is the time guides suggest, when the sun lights the mosaics and facade. If you want a second angle, the Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale looks down on the bell tower and the town roofs, but it needs a steep walk. The harbour pier gives a view of the facade and tower between the pink and yellow waterfront buildings.
text.geographic_location: The cathedral stands on Piazza del Duomo in Amalfi, at the top of its wide flight of steps.
text.directions_text: Make your way to Piazza del Duomo in Amalfi. From there it is about 1 minute on foot to the cathedral itself. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the whole facade, bell tower and steps into one frame from close up. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural look with less stretching at the edges. Use the telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for details such as the mosaics in the pediment and the tiled crown of the tower.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Piazza Duomo (foot of the cathedral steps, facing up toward the facade). The striped facade and bell tower rising above the 62 steps, with the square's fountain and people in the foreground. Facing up toward the facade. From here the striped facade and bell tower rise above the 62 steps, with the square's fountain and people in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line up the edges of the facade and tower with the vertical lines. Hold the phone level, because tilting it upward makes the building lean. Include a little of the fountain or a few people at the bottom to give a sense of scale. For a different view, try the Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale (a steep walk, looking down on the tower and roofs) or the harbour pier (the facade between the waterfront buildings).
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the facade to focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the bright marble and mosaics keep their detail. If the square is busy, take a few shots in a row and pick the one with the clearest foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Late afternoon, when the sun lights the mosaics and facade.

text.access_note: The cathedral is a place of worship, so check the official site before you go for visiting times, dress code and any entry ticket for the interior; the square in front is open to everyone.
claims_not_in_sources: Visitors to a working cathedral are usually expected to dress modestly, with shoulders and knees covered.
The square can be busy in the middle of the day, so people may appear in the foreground.

text.description:
The Museo della Carta is Amalfi's paper museum (the name means exactly that), and it is rank 4 on this map. It is a spot for a quick, calm photo stop rather than a big panorama. The appeal is the building itself, its entrance and any signs or details that tell a passer-by what it is. A photo here works well as a travel-diary picture that says where you have been, and it pairs nicely with wider shots of Amalfi taken elsewhere on your walk.

The phone icon on the map sits right at the museum, so you do not need to hunt for a viewpoint. Stand close, look for the cleanest view of the front, and take a step back if other visitors are in the way. Keep your phone upright for a doorway or façade, and turn it sideways if you want to include the street or surroundings.

If you would like a shot of an interior, exhibit or demonstration, rules on photography inside can differ from place to place, so ask the staff or check the official site before you go. Outside, take your time, tidy up the edges of the frame, and take a few versions so you can choose later.

text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot. Follow the map to the phone icon on the map, which is at the museum itself. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of the entrance. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for signs, plaques or details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Step back along the street if you need more of the façade in the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines and line the doorway or front wall up with the vertical lines so the building looks straight. Leave a little space around the edges, and shoot a wide version and a close detail of the entrance or sign.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the entrance on your screen to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright and the walls look dark or washed out. Wipe the lens first.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Go when the street is quiet so there are fewer people in the frame. Soft daylight usually flatters a building front better than harsh midday sun.

name: Torre dello Ziro
label: Torre dello Ziro
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Veliero del Belvedere' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Belvedere del Veliero' (node/2375662550): point; moved 5 m off buildings.
pin_note: Position from OSM W1098012004 (Salita Torre dello Ziro): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Ruined tower on the cliff with a famous view over Amalfi and Atrani.

text.description:
Torre dello Ziro is a cylindrical ruined tower on a hilltop above Amalfi and Atrani. It is reached by a long trail with plenty of steps, and most walkers set out from Pontone, in Scala. The effort pays off for photographs. The tower is a strong shape on its own, and from near it you can see Amalfi, Atrani and the sea spread out below.

The best-known photo stop is a terrace called Veliero del Belvedere, on the trail branch just before the tower, on the uphill side. Guides recommend it as a stop for the best photos on this trail. From there you get a wide view over the coast and the towns, with the tower in the background. A higher belvedere above the tower may give a wider view including the tower itself. Ask locally to find the exact terrace.

For a second picture, walk the short way to the tower. With the tower in the foreground, Amalfi and Atrani sit behind it with the sea beyond. That gives you a layered shot with a clear foreground, middle and background.

Allow roughly 1.5 to 2.5 hours for the round trip from Pontone. Going inside the tower may not be safe, so check on the day. Treat it as a ruin, look from outside unless you are sure, and take care near edges.
text.geographic_location: On a hilltop above Amalfi and Atrani, on the walking trail that links the two towns, well uphill from the waterfront. Most walkers approach from Pontone, in Scala.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot. The trail usually starts from Pontone (Scala); from there, follow the stair-filled trail up to the tower. Use a hiking app or an offline map, as Google Maps routing has been reported as wrong here. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) on the terrace for the coast-and-towns view. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want to fit in more of the slope and the sea. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pull the tower closer from a distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Veliero del Belvedere (on the trail branch just before the tower, uphill side). A panoramic view over the coast and towns, with the Torre dello Ziro visible in the background. The Veliero del Belvedere terrace is on the trail branch just before the tower, on the uphill side. From the terrace the photo shows a panoramic view over the coast and towns, with Torre dello Ziro visible in the background.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and put the horizon on the upper or lower line, so the coast does not look tilted. Place the tower on a third so it stays visible without dominating the frame. For the alternative, walk to the tower and shoot with it in the foreground and Amalfi, Atrani and the sea behind. A higher belvedere above the tower may give a wider view, so ask locally.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the sky or the sea to set focus, then slide the exposure down slightly so the sky keeps its colour. If the view is wide, try panorama mode and move slowly and steadily.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually suits the coast best. Leave enough daylight to walk back down the steps.

text.access_note: This is an open hillside trail to a ruined tower, but conditions and entry to the tower can change, so ask locally before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Morning or late-afternoon light is usually softer than midday light for coastal views.
Sturdy footwear and some daylight in hand are sensible for a trail with many steps.
Panorama mode works best when the phone is moved slowly and steadily.

name: Piazza Duomo
label: Piazza Duomo
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Piazza Duomo' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Piazza Duomo' (way/191471192): middle (61 m across).
pin_note: Position from OSM W254643211 (Duomo di Amalfi): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: The lively main square below the cathedral stairs.

text.description: Piazza Duomo is the square in front of Amalfi's cathedral, and it works well as a first stop for photos of the town. The cathedral's striped facade rises above a tall staircase of about 62 steps, with the square's fountain in the foreground. Guides often call this the classic postcard angle, and it is easy to see why. The steps lead the eye up to the facade, and the fountain gives the picture a clear foreground. It is also a short, flat walk from the harbour and the bus stop, so it works well as a first stop. The steps are popular with tourists and wedding parties, so you may have to wait a little for a clear frame. Be patient and take a few shots as people move. Late afternoon is the time to aim for, when the light falls on the cathedral's mosaics. If you want a wider view of the whole scene, a seat at a café in the square can give you one. Keep your phone level and use the gridlines so the tall facade does not lean. Take one wide shot to show the square and one closer shot of the facade and steps. Then try a portrait of your group with the fountain behind you.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Amalfi, in the square in front of the cathedral. It is a short, flat walk from the harbour.
text.directions_text: Start from the harbour or the bus stop in the centre of Amalfi and walk the short, flat way to the square. Face east towards the facade. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of the facade. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if the steps and fountain will not both fit. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for details of the mosaics.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Piazza Duomo (foot of the cathedral steps, facing the facade). The striped facade and its tall staircase of about 62 steps, with the piazza's fountain in the foreground. From here you see the striped front of the cathedral and its tall staircase of about 62 steps, with the fountain in the foreground. Walk closer to the steps if you want the foot-of-the-steps angle.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put the fountain low in the frame and let the steps lead up to the facade. Turn on gridlines and hold the phone level, so the building does not lean back. If you want a wider view of the square, a seat at one of the cafés gives a different angle.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the facade to focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the bright stonework looks washed out. Take several shots, because people keep moving on the steps.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Late afternoon, when the light falls on the cathedral's mosaics.

text.access_note: The square is free to visit, but the cathedral is a place of worship, and its opening hours and mass times can block access to the steps, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Holding the phone level and using gridlines helps to keep tall buildings from appearing to lean backwards.
Sliding the exposure down can help when bright stonework looks washed out.
Ultra-wide (0.5x) can fit both the steps and the fountain into one frame when you are standing close.

notes: Fountain in the centre of Piazza Duomo.

text.description:
The Fontana di Sant'Andrea stands in Amalfi's Piazza Duomo, in front of the cathedral, with the cathedral's facade rising directly behind it. That pairing is the reason to stop here. The fountain gives you a lively foreground, and the cathedral gives you a grand backdrop, so one frame can hold both.

The phone icon on the map is at the fountain itself, in the square. From there you can shoot the sculpted basin and statue in detail, with the busy square and the cathedral soft behind. The square is very crowded by day, so expect people in the frame and be ready to wait a moment for a gap.

For a wider view, go to the cathedral staircase, looking down across the square. Guides single this out as the best photo position because the fountain and the facade appear together in one picture. Lonely Planet advises seeing the cathedral from several angles on the square before climbing, so take a few shots from below first, then climb for the wide view.

Both spots are open-air and free to stand in. The climb to the top of the staircase is about 62 steps, so allow a minute and take your time with a phone in your hand.
text.geographic_location: The fountain is in Piazza Duomo in Amalfi, in front of the Cattedrale di Sant'Andrea.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot, so reach it on foot in Amalfi, in Piazza Duomo in front of the cathedral. The fountain is in the square, and the phone icon on the map is at the fountain itself. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

From the cathedral staircase, the default lens (1x) suits the wide view of the fountain and facade. Use telephoto (2x or more) for close shots of the fountain's statue.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. For the wider view, climb the Cattedrale di Sant'Andrea staircase and look down across the square to get the fountain and facade together.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the fountain on the lower third, with the cathedral facade filling the upper part. Keep the phone level so the facade does not lean. Take a close shot at the fountain to show the sculpted basin and statue, then a wider one from the staircase.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the fountain to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the bright facade looks washed out. Take a few frames in a row, as people will move through the shot.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: The square is very crowded by day, so expect people in the shot and be ready to wait a moment for a gap.

name: Chiostro del Paradiso
label: Cloister of Paradise
camera_source: No separate stand-here point: photographed at the spot itself (indoors, from its top, or right in front of it); drawn as the split pin.
pin_note: Position from OSM R18856362 (Chiostro del Paradiso): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: 13th-century cloister with Moorish-style arches next to the cathedral.

text.description:
The Chiostro del Paradiso is a cloister in the old centre of Amalfi: an enclosed courtyard with covered walkways round the edge. It is a good place for a phone camera because the repeating arches give you ready-made lines and frames. You can shoot straight along a walkway so the arches shrink into the distance, or stand at the edge of the open courtyard and frame the arches as a border around the open courtyard.

The phone icon on the map is inside the cloister itself, so you are photographing the place you are standing in rather than something far away. That suits wide, scene-setting shots, and it also suits close detail: a column, a carved capital, a patch of sunlight on old stone.

Take a few minutes to look around before you start shooting. Turn slowly on the spot, because the best view is often behind you. Keep the phone level, with gridlines switched on, so the arches stay straight. If other visitors wander into the frame, wait a moment; people tend to move on quickly, and a figure in the walkway can give a nice sense of scale. A short run of three or four shots from slightly different heights gives you options later.

As this may be a ticketed or managed site, check the official site before you go for access details and any rules on photography.
text.geographic_location: In the historic centre of Amalfi.
text.directions_text: Head for the old centre of Amalfi and use the map to find the cloister. Use the map to reach the centre of Amalfi, then continue on foot to the cloister. The phone icon on the map is at the cloister itself, so there is no extra walk once you are inside. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the arches and the courtyard in one frame; the space is enclosed, so it helps. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural look. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for details such as capitals, columns and carved stone.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. The subject is right where you are standing, so you can turn in any direction and choose your angle.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on gridlines and line up the walkway with a vertical grid line so the arches run straight. Try one shot looking down the length of a covered walkway, and one from the open courtyard using the arches as a frame. Crouch slightly for a more dramatic perspective on the arches.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the brightest part of the courtyard to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sunlit areas keep their detail. The covered walkways will look darker, which adds contrast. If your phone has night mode, it may switch on in the shaded walkways; hold steady for the full exposure.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Earlier or later in the day usually means fewer people and softer light in the courtyard. Midday sun can make harsh contrast between the walkways and the open space, so use the exposure slider if you visit then.

text.access_note: This may be a ticketed or managed site with its own visiting rules, so check the official site before you go.
